answer: Hypothesis: Original studies report larger effect-size estimates than their replications in every domain examined (Social, Cognitive, and Experimental Economics), but the gap is largest in the Social domain. Using relative retention (replication effect ÷ original effect, i.e., relative_es) as the primary metric, replications in Social retain on average only ~28% of the original effect (median 13%), with 11 of 34 studies (32%) even flipping sign, whereas Cognitive retains ~51% (median 65%) and Economics ~66% (median 70%); thus Social Psychology is the domain where original-study effects are most inflated relative to replications. Caveat on metric: on the absolute-difference metric mean(ro − rr) the ranking differs — Cognitive (0.249) > Social (0.223) > Economics (0.196) — so if "larger gap" is read as absolute difference, Cognitive ranks first; the two metrics disagree because Social's original effects are smaller to begin with, so the same relative collapse produces a smaller absolute gap. At the project level the conclusion is consistent: the Psychology project (n=68) shows larger original-vs-replication shrinkage (mean relative_es 0.39, median 0.30; mean ro−rr 0.236) than Experimental Economics (mean relative_es 0.66, median 0.70; mean ro−rr 0.196). One data quirk: for Eitam et al. (Social), rr is stored positive (+0.105) while relative_es is negative (−0.472); treating that rr as negative would slightly widen Social's absolute gap (mean ro−rr 0.223→0.229, median 0.213→0.244) and leave the relative-retention statistics unchanged, so conclusions are unaffected.

On the absolute-difference metric the ranking differs (Cognitive 0.249 > Social 0.223 > Economics 0.196); the two metrics disagree because Social's original effects are smaller, so the same relative collapse yields a smaller absolute gap. The project-level check is consistent: Psychology (mean relative_es 0.39) shrinks more than Experimental Economics (0.66).
payload.workflow: Read the 86-row joined CSV; verified integrity (fiso=atanh(ro), fisr=atanh(rr) to machine precision; relative_es=rr/ro except one flagged row, Eitam et al. where relative_es keeps the replication's sign while rr is stored positive). Computed per discipline (primary) and per project (robustness): mean/median of ro−rr (correlation scale) and fiso−fisr (Fisher-z, robustness), mean/median of relative_es, fraction with ro>rr, sign-flip counts, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and bootstrap 95% CIs. Checked ranking consistency across scales and metrics; ran a sensitivity analysis treating the Eitam rr as negative (widens Social's absolute gap slightly, leaves relative-retention stats unchanged). Saved per-domain tables and the full script as artifacts.
